# Dex (one IdP)

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Identity provider · **Label:** `feature:dex-oidc` · **Epic:** [#16](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/16) · **Tickets:** 6 (5S 1M)

Ship a reference Dex deployment that Warden and agent harnesses trust: one IdP in front of the company directory that issues short-lived ID tokens with groups. Operators get a pinned, documented compose recipe and config that they can point at LDAP, GitHub, Google or upstream OIDC connectors. Warden treats Dex only as a generic OIDC issuer. None of this exists in the repo yet: there is no deploy/compose/dex/, no identity compose file, no OIDC dependency in go.mod, no secret-literal check in scripts/check.sh and no shared identity end-to-end stack. The feature is verified in two layers: static Go tests in test/deploy (no Docker) and the shared L2 identity stack in test/e2e/identity (`make e2e-identity`, W-P1-DEX-04; its tests fail under CI and skip loudly locally when the stack is missing), which p1-identity-contract (W-P1-IDC-03) and p1-sso-roles (W-P1-SSO-07) reuse.

## How we build it

- Dex is only a standard OIDC issuer for Warden. Nothing in internal/ or cmd/ calls Dex-specific APIs; Dex-specific strings live only in deploy/compose/dex/, deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml, scripts/dex-token.sh and docs/identity-dex.md. Any standards-compliant OIDC issuer can replace it.
- Clients (staticClients; secrets via `secretEnv`, never committed): `warden-console` is confidential and used only for CP console login, redirect `<cp-browser-url>/auth/callback`. `warden` is the data-plane audience: confidential, no redirect URIs, never used to log anyone in, with `trustedPeers: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` so those clients can mint tokens whose aud contains `warden`. `agent-harness` is confidential, for server-side harness platforms. `warden-cli` is public (no secret) and device-code only, for `warden identity login` on user machines; it lists the Dex device callback (`<issuer>/device/callback`) in redirectURIs. Splitting console and data-plane clients means a console login token never carries aud `warden`.
- Grants: `oauth2.grantTypes` is set explicitly to authorization_code, refresh_token and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`; `oauth2.responseTypes: [code]`, `oauth2.skipApprovalScreen: true` (all clients are first-party; the approval screen returns HTTP 500 "Approval rejected" with a static client plus a local connector on v2.41.1, and a throwaway IdP does not need it, a note kept as a config comment and a README line). The password grant (`password` in grantTypes plus `oauth2.passwordConnector: ldap`) appears only in the dev recipe file `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml`, which the smoke and e2e tests use. The prod example `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` has no password grant, because it lets a client collect directory passwords and bypasses upstream MFA.
- Scopes: clients must request `openid email profile groups offline_access`, plus `audience:server:client_id:warden` for agent-harness and warden-cli. Without `groups` the token has no groups claim and role and group policy silently see none; without `offline_access` there is no refresh token. With cross-client trust Dex sets aud to the requested peer and azp to the requesting client, so checks are `aud contains warden` and `azp in {agent-harness, warden-cli}`.
- Expiry: `idTokens: 1h`, `signingKeys: 6h`, `deviceRequests: 5m`. Dex keeps previous public keys published until their tokens expire, and the worker verifier (p1-verify-token) refetches JWKS on an unknown kid at most once per 30s, so rotation needs no Warden restart. Refresh tokens: `validIfNotUsedFor: 168h`, `absoluteLifetime: 720h`, rotation on, `reuseInterval: 3s`; clients must serialize refresh (the CLI holds a lock file). Absolute expiry and loss of Dex storage both return `invalid_grant`; later offboarding logic must not treat that alone as a disabled user (see open cross-feature note on p3-offboarding).
- Identity keys: the Dex `sub` is opaque and encodes the connector id together with the upstream user id. The issuer string is permanent too: identity is keyed by (issuer, sub), so changing it later makes every user a new person. Connector `id` values (recipe: `ldap`) are permanent once users exist; renaming one or switching connectors changes every sub and requires re-keying user-scoped state (block list, per-user credentials in the CP-only consent.store keyed by secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) from p3-consent-signin, grants, attribution). The docs show the `federated:id` scope for diagnostics. Group names `warden-admins`, `warden-editors`, `warden-viewers`, `eng` are recipe defaults that `console.roles` and group policy map, not a contract.
- Dev directory: an OpenLDAP container seeded from `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif` with `{SSHA}` password hashes only (dev-only, path-allowlisted in the secret check). The LDAP connector uses userSearch and groupSearch so `groups` comes from the directory, and its bindPW comes from env. Dex static passwords are not used because they cannot carry groups. Commented examples cover GitHub (orgs/teams, `teamNameField`), Google and upstream OIDC, with a table showing groups source, required scope and whether refresh re-checks the upstream user.
- Issuer and transport (split-horizon): the dev recipe issuer is `http://localhost:5556/dex`, the one public string in every token, discovery document and redirect. Dex is published on 127.0.0.1:5556, so browsers and the CLI on the host reach it with no hosts entry; tests and the L2 helpers call `http://localhost:5556` directly and there is no test-only dialer. Containers that must reach Dex (the CP and workers) cannot use `localhost`, so they set the optional internal issuer URL `http://dex:5556` (`console.oidc.internalIssuerURL` in W-P1-SSO-02, `identity.internalIssuerURL` in W-P1-VRFY-08): server-side OIDC calls (discovery, JWKS, token exchange) whose origin equals the issuer's origin are sent to the internal origin (W-P1-VRFY-12), changing only scheme, host and port of the TCP destination; the issuer string, path, headers and body never change, and browser redirects and tokens keep the public issuer. A plain-http issuer is accepted only when an internal issuer URL is set (the dev profile); otherwise https is required, and there is no insecure flag. Production uses one https issuer reachable by everyone and leaves `internalIssuerURL` unset.
- Networks: Dex joins `cp-net` (CP and workers fetch discovery and JWKS through the internal origin `http://dex:5556`) and a new `idp-net` (`internal: true`) shared with LDAP. LDAP has no host port and joins only idp-net. Dex is never attached to an agent `internal: true` network. Tokens are obtained by the harness or host outside the agent sandbox; if an agent must refresh in-sandbox it goes through its worker with an explicit allow rule for the Dex host, a documented trade-off that keeps default-deny intact. Upstream connector examples need an extra egress network, shown commented. The identity file declares every network it uses, so it works standalone and merged with `-f` into docker-compose.control-plane.yml or docker-compose.yml.
- Image pinned by tag and digest: `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.41.1@sha256:...` is the tested baseline (it replaces "latest stable at least 2 weeks old"); a later bump is its own change that re-runs the runtime proofs (W-P1-DEX-06); OpenLDAP pinned the same way; both run as the image's non-root user where the image supports it.
- Storage and ops: sqlite3 on the named volume `dex-data` in dev (single replica only). Production uses Postgres or Kubernetes CRD storage with at least 2 replicas and backups; losing storage invalidates every session and refresh token. `telemetry.http: 0.0.0.0:5558` serves health and Prometheus metrics on cp-net only; `logger: {level: info, format: json}`, never debug in prod. A compose healthcheck gates dependents if the pinned image ships a probe tool, otherwise clients rely on retry.
- Degraded modes (documented): Dex down means console login fails (use p1-breakglass) while issued tokens stay valid until exp; a worker that cannot fetch JWKS records `identity_status=unverified` (reason jwks_unavailable) and still allows the request in P1 attribute mode; LDAP down means new logins and refreshes fail; clock skew over 60s produces `expired`, so NTP is required. Alert on spikes in `warden_identity_verify_total{result=~"invalid|unverified"}` (the Prometheus name of the worker instrument `warden.identity.verify.total`) and on Dex health.
- Secret hygiene: new `scripts/check-secrets.sh`, called from `scripts/check.sh`, fails if any file under deploy/compose/dex/ or the identity compose file has a `secret:`, `bindPW:` or `clientSecret:` value that is not an env reference, and allowlists only `seed.ldif` (hashes). Compose uses `${VAR:?}` so missing secrets fail fast. No token, secret or password appears in logs, test output or docs.
- Verification layers: static Go tests in test/deploy (config and compose shape, secret-literal script, token script against a fake token endpoint) need no Docker and run in scripts/check.sh. Everything that needs real Dex or OpenLDAP (issuer string seen from host and container, token claims, device code, restart survival) runs in the shared L2 identity stack in test/e2e/identity (`make e2e-identity-up`, `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=...`, CI job `e2e`). `test/integration` holds only TestSingleBinary and gets no Dex test; there is no WARDEN_IT_DEX switch.
- Limits referenced by the docs: a token is at most 16 KiB; the CONNECT request line is capped at 8 KiB and the whole header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline (already enforced on main, 431 with reason malformed_connect and detail headers_too_large). groupSearch must be scoped so tokens stay well below these limits.
- Logout is local: console logout deletes the Warden session only. The Dex session remains, so the next login can be silent, and no `id_token_hint` is sent because no IdP token is stored. Removing a person's access is the block list's job (W-P1-BLOCK-07, W-P1-BLOCK-05), not logout's. Stack gate: when the identity stack is missing, the L2 identity tests fail under `CI=true` and skip with a loud `BLOCKED` message only locally, so a CI skip can never read as a pass.

## Done when

With `make e2e-identity-up` (Dex and OpenLDAP, both pinned by tag and digest, dev config, merged with the existing control-plane and e2e compose files): (1) `/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the same issuer string `http://localhost:5556/dex` from the host (published port, no hosts entry, no test-only dialer) and from a container on cp-net through `http://dex:5556`, and a token minted for a host client verifies on a worker configured with `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` (W-P1-IDC-03); (2) `scripts/dex-token.sh` for a seeded warden-admins user via `agent-harness` returns an ID token with aud containing `warden`, azp=`agent-harness`, groups containing `warden-admins` and exp-iat=3600; (3) the public `warden-cli` client gets a device_code and user_code; (4) the prod config has no password grant (asserted by `go test ./test/deploy`); (5) after `docker compose restart dex` existing tokens still verify against JWKS and the refresh token still works; (6) the identity file validates merged with docker-compose.control-plane.yml (`go test ./test/deploy` and `docker compose config -q`); (7) `scripts/check.sh` passes with its secret-literal stage; (8) docs/identity-dex.md (split-horizon, issuer permanence, local-only logout) config snippets parse against internal/config and its `run` blocks execute as written on the L2 stack. Checks (1), (2), (3), (5) and (8) run with `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDex`; the rest run in the default gate.

### 1/6 · W-P1-DEX-01

**Add reference Dex config with console, data-plane, harness and CLI clients**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#17](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/17)

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16) ships the reference Dex IdP that p1-verify-token, p1-sso-roles and p1-identity-contract test against. This is the foundation ticket (#17): configuration files, a secret-literal check and a static Go test, with no container started. It has no dependencies. Siblings: W-P1-DEX-02 (#18) the pinned compose recipe and seeded LDAP, W-P1-DEX-05 the token script, W-P1-DEX-04 the shared L2 identity stack, W-P1-DEX-06 the runtime proofs, W-P1-DEX-03 (#19) the operator docs. Out of scope here: images and digests, compose files, LDAP seed data, token fetching (DEX-02/05) and anything that needs a running Dex (DEX-06).

What to build: Add the Dex configuration files that every later identity ticket builds on: a prod-shaped `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` (https issuer placeholder) and a dev recipe `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml` that differs only by enabling the password grant, the LDAP insecure transport and the dev issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` (with the device callback derived from it). They define the four static clients (`warden-console`, `warden`, `agent-harness`, `warden-cli`), explicit grant types, expiry, the LDAP connector with a permanent id, telemetry and logging. A static Go test and a secret-literal check make the ticket testable without running Dex; runtime checks arrive with the compose recipe in W-P1-DEX-02. The dev issuer is split-horizon: Dex is published on 127.0.0.1:5556, so browsers and the CLI on the host use `http://localhost:5556/dex` with no hosts entry, while containers that must reach Dex set an internal issuer URL (`http://dex:5556`, see W-P1-VRFY-12). No Go package or existing compose file changes.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `scripts/check.sh` and `tools/checkreport`; request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- New `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` (prod-shaped): issuer `https://dex.example.com/dex` as a clearly marked placeholder (production uses one https issuer reachable by browsers, CLIs, the CP and workers alike, so no internal issuer URL is needed), `web.http: 0.0.0.0:5556`, storage sqlite3 at `/var/dex/dex.db`, `oauth2.responseTypes: [code]`, `oauth2.skipApprovalScreen: true` with a config comment saying why (the approval screen returns HTTP 500 "Approval rejected" with a static client plus a local connector on Dex v2.41.1, and a first-party throwaway IdP does not need it), `oauth2.grantTypes` = authorization_code, refresh_token, `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`; no `password` grant and no `passwordConnector`.
- staticClients: `warden-console` (secretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirect `https://localhost:7070/auth/callback`, unchanged); `warden` (secretEnv WARDEN_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, no redirectURIs, trustedPeers [agent-harness, warden-cli]); `agent-harness` (secretEnv HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET); `warden-cli` (`public: true`, redirectURIs include the Dex device callback `<issuer>/device/callback`, which Dex derives from the issuer: `http://localhost:5556/dex/device/callback` in the dev file, the placeholder https issuer's callback in the prod-shaped file). No `secret:` literal anywhere.
- expiry: idTokens 1h, signingKeys 6h, deviceRequests 5m, refreshTokens {validIfNotUsedFor 168h, absoluteLifetime 720h, reuseInterval 3s, disableRotation false}.
- LDAP connector with permanent `id: ldap` and a comment that the id is permanent because it is encoded into every user's sub: host ldap:389, bindDN, bindPW from env, userSearch (username uid, idAttr uid, emailAttr mail, nameAttr cn), groupSearch (userMatchers DN -> member, nameAttr cn). `insecureNoSSL: true` only in the dev file, with a comment that prod uses ldaps or StartTLS with rootCA.
- New `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml`: issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` (Dex is published on 127.0.0.1:5556; containers reach it through an internal issuer URL, W-P1-VRFY-12) and the matching `warden-cli` device callback, `password` added to grantTypes, `oauth2.passwordConnector: ldap`, and the LDAP insecure transport; everything else identical. Both files carry a header comment naming which one is dev-only, and both carry the approval-screen comment of the first requirement.
- `telemetry.http: 0.0.0.0:5558` and `logger: {level: info, format: json}` in both files; debug level forbidden.
- New `scripts/check-secrets.sh` called from `scripts/check.sh` as stage `secrets (no literals in deploy/compose/dex)`: fails when `secret:`, `bindPW:` or `clientSecret:` under deploy/compose/dex/ or deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml is not `$VAR` or `${VAR...}`, and allowlists only `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif`.
- New `deploy/compose/dex/README.md` explaining each field, the required scope set, why the console and data-plane clients are split, why warden-cli is public and why the password grant is dev-only. It has a 'Pinned release' section naming the tested baseline `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.41.1` (W-P1-DEX-02 adds the digest; a later bump is its own change that re-runs W-P1-DEX-06). It has a short split-horizon paragraph: the dev issuer is `http://localhost:5556/dex` for browsers and host CLIs; the CP and workers run in containers where `localhost` is themselves, so they set `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` and Warden sends server-side discovery, JWKS and token-exchange calls for the issuer's origin to that internal origin while the issuer string, path, headers and tokens stay public; production uses one https issuer and leaves it unset. It states, next to the permanent connector id rule, that the issuer string is permanent too: identity is keyed by (issuer, sub), so changing it later makes every user a new person (block list entries, attribution and per-user secrets keyed by `secrets.UserKey(iss, sub)` stop matching). It has one line saying why `skipApprovalScreen: true` stays: the approval screen returns HTTP 500 ("Approval rejected") with a static client plus a local connector on v2.41.1 and a throwaway IdP does not need it. Env expansion is a decision, not an open question: Dex expands environment variables in connector config only when the top-level `expandEnv: true` is set in recent releases. The implementer verifies this against the v2.41.1 docs. If it works, the LDAP connector uses `bindPW: $LDAP_BIND_PW` with `expandEnv: true`; if it is unsupported, `bindPW` comes from a mounted file or from an entrypoint-rendered config. The README records which was chosen and why, and the config tests assert the chosen form.
- `scripts/check-secrets.sh` is wired as a real gate stage named `secrets`: add the banner stage to scripts/check.sh AND the stage definition to tools/checkreport/runner.go (stage list, so `scripts/check.sh --list-stages` and the --json report include it), with a tools/checkreport test. The script scans `${ROOT:-.}` so a test can point it at a temp tree.
- New package `test/deploy` (build-tag free, covered by the `testutil` class `test/**` in architecture.yaml; it needs at least one _test.go). It adds no Go module: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 is already in go.mod.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `scripts/check.sh` and `tools/checkreport`; request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Read the Dex v2.41.1 config reference for staticClients, secretEnv, public clients, device flow redirect, grantTypes, refreshTokens and env expansion.
2. Write new `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` with the https issuer placeholder, storage, oauth2, expiry, telemetry, logger, the four static clients and the LDAP connector as listed in the requirements.
3. Write new `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml` as a copy that changes only the issuer (`http://localhost:5556/dex`) and the `warden-cli` device callback, and adds the password grant, `passwordConnector: ldap` and the LDAP insecure transport.
4. Add new `test/deploy/dex_config_test.go` (package deploy, uses gopkg.in/yaml.v3 already in go.mod) with `TestDexReferenceConfig`: parses both files, asserts the dev issuer is exactly `http://localhost:5556/dex`, the prod-shaped issuer starts with `https://`, the device callback equals `<issuer>/device/callback` in each file, the raw files contain the approval-screen comment (`Approval rejected`), expiry values, client set, trustedPeers, `warden-cli` public with the device callback, `warden` with no redirectURIs, connector id `ldap`, no `secret` field on any client, logger level not debug, and that the prod file has no `password` grant or passwordConnector.
5. Add the same test's diff check: the two files differ only in issuer, the warden-cli device callback, oauth2.grantTypes, oauth2.passwordConnector and the LDAP insecure fields.
6. Add new `scripts/check-secrets.sh` and call it from `scripts/check.sh` after the roadmap stage, with a banner like the existing stages.
7. Write new `deploy/compose/dex/README.md`.
8. Add the `secrets` stage to tools/checkreport/runner.go with its test, and add `TestCheckSecretsScript` to test/deploy: it copies a fixture tree to a temp dir, runs `ROOT=<tmp> scripts/check-secrets.sh`, and asserts exit 0 for env references and for seed.ldif hashes, and non-zero (naming the file and line, never the value) for `secret: abc`, `bindPW: hunter2` and `clientSecret: x` literals.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestDexReferenceConfig` passes and fails if any asserted field (idTokens 1h, signingKeys 6h, trustedPeers, warden-cli public, connector id ldap) is changed.
- [ ] The test fails if `password` appears in config.yaml grantTypes or if config.yaml sets passwordConnector.
- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestCheckSecretsScript` passes: the script exits non-zero (naming file and line, not the value) when a temp tree has `secret: abc`, `bindPW: hunter2` or `clientSecret: x`, and exits 0 for `$VAR`/`${VAR...}` references and the seed.ldif allowlist. Without the script the test fails (red first).
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh --list-stages` prints a `secrets` stage and `go test ./tools/checkreport` passes; `scripts/check.sh` runs the stage and passes.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only origin/main -- deploy/compose/*.yml internal/` prints nothing (only new files under deploy/compose/dex/, scripts/, test/deploy/, tools/checkreport and scripts/check.sh change).
- [ ] The README names the pinned Dex tag `v2.41.1` and the env-expansion decision, and `go test ./test/deploy -run TestDexReferenceConfig` asserts the connector's bindPW form matches that decision.
- [ ] The dev issuer, split-horizon and permanence are checkable: `go test ./test/deploy -run TestDexReferenceConfig` fails (red first) when the dev issuer is not `http://localhost:5556/dex` or the prod-shaped issuer is not https; `grep -n 'localhost:5556' deploy/compose/dex/README.md` and `grep -n 'internalIssuerURL' deploy/compose/dex/README.md` both match; `grep -nEi 'issuer.*(permanent|never change)' deploy/compose/dex/README.md` matches; `grep -n 'Approval rejected' deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml deploy/compose/dex/README.md` lists all three files.

### 2/6 · W-P1-DEX-02

**Add identity compose recipe with pinned Dex and seeded LDAP**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#18](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/18)

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16) ships a reference Dex IdP. W-P1-DEX-01 (#17) wrote the Dex config files; this ticket (#18) wraps them in `deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml` with a pinned Dex, a pinned OpenLDAP and a seeded directory. It was split from the original M ticket #18: the token script moved to W-P1-DEX-05, every check that needs a running Dex moved to W-P1-DEX-06 (L2), and the CP, worker and agent containers for end-to-end tests live in the shared stack W-P1-DEX-04. The old `test/integration/dex_recipe_test.go` behind WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 is dropped: test/integration now holds only TestSingleBinary and behaviour tests live in L1 and L2. Out of scope here: any Go package, any worker or CP code, token fetching, runtime proof. Static checks only.

What to build: the compose file, `seed.ldif`, `.env.example` and a static Go test `TestIdentityComposePinned`. The file works standalone and merged with docker-compose.control-plane.yml or docker-compose.yml, and never attaches Dex or LDAP to an agent network.

**Requirements**

- Service `dex`: image `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.41.1@sha256:<digest>`: v2.41.1 is the tested baseline, replacing "latest stable at least 2 weeks old"; the digest is resolved with registry access at implementation time (`docker buildx imagetools inspect` or `crane digest`) and written, with the resolution date, into the README 'Pinned release' section, which also says that a later Dex bump is its own change (new tag and digest) that re-runs W-P1-DEX-06 (`make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDex`). The service name `dex` on cp-net gives containers the internal origin `http://dex:5556` (used as `internalIssuerURL` by the CP and worker configs); the host reaches the same container at `http://localhost:5556` through the published 127.0.0.1 port, which is the dev issuer origin. It mounts `dex/config.dev.yaml` read-only, uses named volume `dex-data:/var/dex`, publishes only `127.0.0.1:5556:5556` and joins cp-net and idp-net. Telemetry port 5558 is not published.
- Service `ldap`: OpenLDAP pinned by tag and digest the same way (the OpenLDAP tag is chosen at implementation time), seeded from new `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif`, joins only idp-net, has no `ports`, admin password from `${LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?}`. Both images run as the image's non-root user where the image supports it.
- seed.ldif: groups warden-admins, warden-editors, warden-viewers, eng (groupOfNames); users alice (warden-admins, eng), bob (warden-editors), carol (warden-viewers), dave (eng only, for the 403 role test). Passwords are stored only as `{SSHA}` hashes (generated with slappasswd), marked dev-only in a header comment. seed.ldif is the only path allowlisted by scripts/check-secrets.sh.
- Secrets via `${WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${WARDEN_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${LDAP_BIND_PW:?}`; new committed `deploy/compose/dex/.env.example` holds placeholder values and the dev test passwords (a root .env is already gitignored). Missing secrets fail fast through `:?`.
- Networks declared in the file: `cp-net` (bridge, the same name as in docker-compose.control-plane.yml so they merge) and `idp-net` (`internal: true`). Dex is on cp-net and idp-net only and is never on an agent network; LDAP is on idp-net only. Upstream connector networks appear only as commented examples.
- Healthchecks: LDAP via ldapsearch; Dex via its telemetry health endpoint if the pinned image ships a probe tool, else none and clients retry. Dex `depends_on` ldap with `condition: service_healthy`.
- Back-compat: opt-in file. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control-plane.yml are unchanged (`git diff --name-only origin/main -- deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml` prints nothing).
- New static test `TestIdentityComposePinned` in test/deploy/dex_config_test.go (package already created by W-P1-DEX-01), parsing the YAML with gopkg.in/yaml.v3: every `image:` matches `:[^@]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}` and the dex image tag is exactly `v2.41.1`; the port in config.dev.yaml's issuer equals the published host port; ldap has no `ports`; dex publishes only 5556 and binds 127.0.0.1; dex's networks are exactly {cp-net, idp-net} and no service in any deploy/compose/*.yml lists both dex and an agent network; network names `cp-net` match docker-compose.control-plane.yml; every secret is a `${VAR:?}` reference; the file passes scripts/check-secrets.sh.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write new `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif` and generate the {SSHA} hashes with slappasswd; record the dev plaintexts only in `.env.example`.
2. Write new `deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml` with services dex and ldap, volume dex-data, networks cp-net and idp-net, healthchecks and env-sourced secrets.
3. Resolve and write the image digest for `dex:v2.41.1` and the chosen OpenLDAP tag; update the 'Pinned release' section of deploy/compose/dex/README.md.
4. Add `TestIdentityComposePinned` to test/deploy/dex_config_test.go, run it, then mutate the file (drop a digest, add `ports` to ldap, add `5558:5558`) and confirm each mutation fails the test.
5. Run `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml config -q` with the .env.example values, and the same with docker-compose.yml.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestIdentityComposePinned` passes, and fails (red first) when an image loses its digest, the dex tag is not v2.41.1, ldap gains `ports`, dex publishes 5558 or joins another network.
- [ ] `set -a; . deploy/compose/dex/.env.example; set +a; docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml config -q` exits 0, and the same with deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml in place of the control-plane file (needs the docker CLI compose plugin, no daemon).
- [ ] `scripts/check-secrets.sh` exits 0 on the tree with the new compose file and seed.ldif.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only origin/main -- deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml` prints nothing.
- [ ] Runtime facts (same issuer string from the host at localhost:5556 and from a container at dex:5556, token claims for alice and dave, device code, restart survival) are NOT checked here; they are proven by W-P1-DEX-06: `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDex`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 3/6 · W-P1-DEX-03

**Document Dex as Warden's IdP with connector, failure-mode and prod guidance**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#19](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/19)

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16). This docs ticket (#19) is the operator guide for running Dex as Warden's IdP: token flow, client split, scopes, group naming, connectors, issuer and network rules, key rotation, degraded modes and the production checklist. It cites exact CP and worker config keys, so it depends on W-P1-SSO-02 (console block) and W-P1-VRFY-08 (identity block); it documents the 16 KiB token cap that W-P1-VRFY-01 creates (hence that dependency), the split-horizon issuer rule of W-P1-VRFY-12 and the local-only logout of W-P1-SSO-09 (hence those dependencies); it also quotes limits from W-P1-VRFY-02 and commands from the DEX-02/05 recipe, and its `run` blocks execute on the W-P1-DEX-04 stack. This ticket-level dependency on later P1 features is intentional and accepted: p1-sso-roles and p1-verify-token depend on p1-dex, so the feature-level depends_on_items stays empty to avoid a cycle, and this docs ticket merges after those tickets. Siblings: DEX-01 (config), DEX-02 (compose), DEX-05 (token script), DEX-04 (L2 stack), DEX-06 (runtime proofs). Out of scope: any code, Kubernetes manifests, the identity contract (W-P1-IDC-01).

What to build: docs/identity-dex.md plus links, and two tests that keep the doc honest. Warden only needs a standards OIDC issuer, and the doc says so plainly.

**Requirements**

- Token flow: harness or CLI -> Dex (device code on warden-cli, or authorization code on agent-harness) -> ID token with aud containing `warden` and azp of the requesting client -> `Proxy-Authorization: Basic session:<token>` or `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer` to the worker, verified by internal/identity. Tokens are obtained outside the agent sandbox; in-sandbox refresh only through the worker with an explicit allow rule.
- Client and scope section: the four clients, why console and data-plane clients are separate, trustedPeers direction, secretEnv names, redirect URIs as the browser sees them, and the required scope set including `groups` and `offline_access`.
- Group and key section: recipe groups mapped through `console.roles.{admin,editor,viewer}` and `console.oidc.{issuer,internalIssuerURL}` (W-P1-SSO-02) and the worker `identity:` keys `defaultMode`, `issuer`, `internalIssuerURL`, `audience`, `allowedAZP` and the per-agent `agents[].identity` field (W-P1-VRFY-08) by exact name; connector claim shapes differ (LDAP cn vs GitHub `org:team`); connector `id` is permanent because it is encoded into sub, with `federated:id` for diagnostics; the issuer string is permanent too (next requirement).
- Connector table: LDAP (ldaps or StartTLS with rootCA in prod), GitHub (orgs, teams, `teamNameField`), Google (groups need a service account), upstream OIDC; columns for groups source, required scope and whether refresh re-checks the upstream user.
- Issuer, transport and network rules (split-horizon): the issuer is one public string, byte-identical in every token, discovery document and redirect. Dev and demo: `http://localhost:5556/dex` (Dex is published on 127.0.0.1:5556), so the browser and the CLI on the host need no hosts entry and no `/etc/hosts` edit. Containers cannot reach `localhost:5556` (inside a container it is the container itself), so the CP and workers set the optional `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` (`console.oidc.internalIssuerURL`, `identity.internalIssuerURL`): server-side OIDC calls (discovery, JWKS, token exchange) whose origin equals the issuer's origin are sent to the internal origin, changing only scheme, host and port of the TCP destination; the issuer string, path, headers and body never change, browser redirects and every token keep the public issuer. A plain-http issuer is accepted only when an internal issuer URL is set (the dev profile); otherwise https is required. Production: one https issuer reachable by browsers, CLIs, the CP and workers alike, with `internalIssuerURL` unset. Every command meant to be executed uses `http://localhost:5556` directly (no `curl --resolve`, no hosts entry). Dex sits on cp-net and idp-net, never on agent networks; upstream connectors need an egress network.
- Issuer permanence, stated next to the permanent connector id rule: identity is keyed by (issuer, sub), so changing the issuer string later makes every user a new person: block list entries, attribution and per-user secrets keyed by `secrets.UserKey(iss, sub)` stop matching. Choose the final public issuer before real users exist; moving Dex behind a new hostname means keeping the old issuer string or re-keying that state.
- Logout is local: console logout (`POST /auth/logout`, W-P1-SSO-09) deletes the Warden session only. The Dex session remains, so the next login can be silent, and no `id_token_hint` is sent because no IdP token is stored. Removing a person's access is the block list's job (W-P1-BLOCK-07 for console login and sessions, W-P1-BLOCK-05 for sessions open when a block lands), not logout's.
- Tested baseline: the doc names `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.41.1` (tag plus digest, W-P1-DEX-02) as the version the recipe and the L2 proofs were tested on; a later bump is its own change that re-runs W-P1-DEX-06.
- Failure modes and rotation: Dex down, LDAP down, JWKS unavailable at worker start, clock skew over 60s, storage loss, refresh absolute expiry and reuse; signingKeys 6h with JWKS refetch on unknown kid at most once per 30s; metrics to alert on; p1-breakglass for console access.
- Prod checklist: https issuer, Postgres or Kubernetes CRD storage with at least 2 replicas (sqlite3 is single replica), backups, password grant off, logger not debug, expiry values, secrets from a secret manager or Kubernetes Secret, groupSearch scoped so tokens stay well under the worker limits: a token is at most 16 KiB (W-P1-VRFY-01), and the CONNECT request line is capped at 8 KiB and the whole header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s deadline (already enforced on main; overflow gets 431, deny reason malformed_connect, detail headers_too_large). Kubernetes guidance is prose only; no manifest is added to deploy/k8s in this phase.
- No real secrets, tokens or passwords in the doc; examples show placeholders and decoded claims only.
- Machine-checked: fenced `yaml` blocks tagged `warden-cp` and `warden-worker` are parsed by a new test `TestIdentityDexDocSnippets` in test/deploy/identity_dex_doc_test.go with the strict config loaders (config.LoadConsole and the worker Policy loader, KnownFields on), and fenced shell blocks tagged `run` are executed in order by `TestDexDocRunBlocks` in test/e2e/identity on the W-P1-DEX-04 stack.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write new `docs/identity-dex.md` with sections for token flow, clients and scopes, groups and keys, connectors, issuer and networks, rotation and failure modes, and prod checklist.
2. Copy the exact key names from `internal/config/console.go` (W-P1-SSO-02) and `internal/config/identity.go` (`IdentitySettings`, W-P1-VRFY-08) as merged on main.
3. Add an example CP config snippet with `console.oidc.clientID: warden-console`, `clientSecretEnv: WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`, `redirectURL: https://localhost:7070/auth/callback`, `issuer: http://localhost:5556/dex` and `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` marked dev-only split-horizon (plus an https production variant with no internalIssuerURL), and a worker `identity:` snippet with `audience: warden` and `allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` so tokens minted for any other client are rejected.
4. Tag every shell block that should run with ```sh run, use `http://localhost:5556` directly in the commands (no hosts entry, no `--resolve`), and add `TestDexDocRunBlocks` to test/e2e/identity (build tag e2e) that extracts and runs them in order against the stack from W-P1-DEX-04 and the token script from W-P1-DEX-05.
5. Link the doc from README.md, docs/control-plane.md, docs/setup-guide.md and deploy/compose/dex/README.md.
6. Add test/deploy/identity_dex_doc_test.go (`TestIdentityDexDocSnippets`).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestIdentityDexDocSnippets` passes: every `warden-cp` and `warden-worker` yaml block parses under strict loading, and the test fails (red first) when a key in the doc is renamed (for example `allowedAZP` to `allowedAzp`).
- [ ] `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDexDocRunBlocks` passes: every `run` block in docs/identity-dex.md exits 0 in order against the L2 identity stack and prints the output shown.
- [ ] `grep -nE 'console\.roles|console\.oidc|identity\.(defaultMode|issuer|internalIssuerURL|audience|allowedAZP)' docs/identity-dex.md` lists only keys that exist in internal/config on main, and `go test ./internal/config/...` passes.
- [ ] The doc contains a prod checklist (https issuer, persistent HA storage, backups, password grant off, expiry values) and a failure-modes section, and warns that changing a connector id changes sub: `grep -c 'connector' docs/identity-dex.md` is non-zero and `grep -i 'password grant' docs/identity-dex.md` matches.
- [ ] The doc quotes the real limits: `grep -E '8 KiB|64 KiB|malformed_connect' docs/identity-dex.md` matches and `grep -E '32 KiB|100 lines' docs/identity-dex.md` prints nothing.
- [ ] The doc contains no secret or raw token: `scripts/check-secrets.sh` passes and `grep -E 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' docs/identity-dex.md` prints nothing. The doc names no product other than ones Warden integrates with (Dex and its LDAP, GitHub, Google and generic OIDC connectors): `grep -niE "keycloak|okta|auth0|azure ad|entra|authentik|zitadel|onelogin|ping ?identity|cognito" docs/identity-dex.md` prints nothing.
- [ ] The doc is linked from README.md, docs/control-plane.md, docs/setup-guide.md and deploy/compose/dex/README.md: `grep -l 'identity-dex.md' README.md docs/control-plane.md docs/setup-guide.md deploy/compose/dex/README.md` lists all four.
- [ ] Split-horizon, permanence and logout are documented and the old guidance is gone: `grep -ci 'allowInsecure[I]ssuer' docs/identity-dex.md` prints 0; `grep -n 'internalIssuerURL' docs/identity-dex.md` and `grep -n 'http://localhost:5556/dex' docs/identity-dex.md` match; `grep -n '/etc/hosts' docs/identity-dex.md | grep -vc 'no /etc/hosts'` prints 0 (the only mention is "no /etc/hosts edit needed"); `grep -nE 'issuer.*(permanent|never change)' docs/identity-dex.md` matches; `grep -nE 'logout.*(Warden session|local)' docs/identity-dex.md` and `grep -n 'id_token_hint' docs/identity-dex.md` match; `grep -n 'v2.41.1' docs/identity-dex.md` matches.
- [ ] `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

### 4/6 · W-P1-DEX-04

**Add the shared L2 identity e2e stack with Dex, a CP, an attribute-mode worker and a curl agent**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16). Three later tickets need real Dex, a real control plane, a real worker and a real agent container: W-P1-IDC-03 (curl-agent attribution smoke), W-P1-IDC-07 (`identity exec`) and W-P1-SSO-07 (console SSO). Without a shared stack each would invent the same compose files, certs, port handling and helpers. This ticket (new, created by the P1 split pass; it replaces the earlier stub) builds that stack once, as an L2 test layer (`test/e2e/identity`, build tag `e2e`, `make e2e-identity`). Behaviour tests for identity attribution already run in-process on L1 (test/harness, W-P1-VRFY-05); this stack exists only for what needs real containers or real Dex. It depends on W-P1-DEX-02 (the Dex+LDAP recipe). It deliberately ships NO identity or console block in the worker/CP configs: W-P1-IDC-03 adds the worker `identity:` block and W-P1-SSO-07 adds the CP `console:` block, each editing its own config file, so this ticket merges before the verifier and the console exist. Out of scope: the identity behaviour tests (IDC-03/07, SSO-07), the Dex runtime proofs (W-P1-DEX-06).

Split-horizon: Dex is reached at `http://localhost:5556` from the host (its published port, the dev issuer origin) and as `http://dex:5556` from the CP and worker containers, which the later tickets configure with `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556`; agent-1 has no route to Dex. There is no test-only dialer and no hosts entry.

What to build: the stack is the existing e2e stack (docker-compose.control-plane.yml + docker-compose.e2e.yml: CP, workers, fake upstream on a pinned IP, internal agent networks, hermeticity self-check) plus the Dex+LDAP recipe (docker-compose.identity.yml) plus a small override. It uses the same compose project (`warden-e2e`) and host ports as `make e2e` (CP 7070, recorder 8081, worker admin 9091/9092), so the two stacks are mutually exclusive and run one after the other; `redirectURL https://localhost:7070/auth/callback` of the Dex `warden-console` client forces CP port 7070.

Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`; request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Requirements**

- New `deploy/compose/docker-compose.e2e-identity.yml`, an override merged as `-f docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f docker-compose.e2e.yml -f docker-compose.identity.yml -f docker-compose.e2e-identity.yml`. It (a) gives dex the extra `published` network (Docker Engine 29 skips published ports on internal-only containers; same trick as the base e2e file) and publishes `127.0.0.1:5556`; (b) points worker-1 at new `configs/config.e2e-identity-worker.yaml` and the control plane at new `configs/config.e2e-identity-cp.yaml`, both copies of the base e2e configs with NO identity or console block; (c) passes `WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET` and the other Dex env values to the CP and workers (the CP and worker containers reach Dex as `http://dex:5556`; their identity and console blocks, added by IDC-03 and SSO-07, set `internalIssuerURL: http://dex:5556` because `localhost` inside a container is the container); (d) starts the CP with `--state-dir /data` on a named volume; (e) makes agent-1 able to run the warden CLI: an init service copies the static `warden` binary from the warden image into a shared read-only volume mounted at `/opt/warden` in agent-1 (no new image is built); (f) keeps agent-1 on its internal-only network with Dex unreachable from it.
- Hermeticity: `test/e2e/hermeticity.sh` must still pass with Dex and LDAP in the stack (neither can complete a round trip to a public IP); extend the script's container list rather than skipping the new containers.
- Makefile: new phony targets `e2e-identity-up` (brings the merged stack up with `up --build --wait`, using `deploy/compose/dex/.env.example` values unless the caller exports others, then runs hermeticity.sh; fails fast with a clear message when the `warden-e2e` project already has running containers), `e2e-identity-down` (`down -v`), `e2e-identity` (`go test -tags e2e -count=1 -timeout 20m ./test/e2e/identity/ -v`) and `e2e-identity-scenario NAME=<regexp>` (same with `-run`). `make e2e` and `make e2e-scenario` keep running only ./test/e2e/ and are unchanged.
- New Go package `test/e2e/identity` (every file `//go:build e2e`, so default `go test ./...` and scripts/check.sh never touch Docker; the `test/**` path is already class `testutil`): `TestMain` modelled on test/e2e/stack_test.go (`E2E_STACK_RUNNING=1` and `E2E_KEEP_STACK=1` honoured, runs `make e2e-identity-up` and `e2e-identity-down` when Docker is available) that records why the stack is unavailable instead of exiting, see the blocked-not-passed requirement; reuse the constants and helpers of test/harness/compose instead of re-declaring ports and service names.
- Helpers in test/e2e/identity (used by IDC-03/07, SSO-07, GPOL-14, OPS1-10, CSIG-07, DEX-03/06): a `dexURL` constant `http://localhost:5556/dex` and a plain `http.Client` with a timeout for the host side (there is NO `dexClient`, NO `DialContext` mapping and NO /etc/hosts entry: the host reaches Dex's published port directly); `dexToken(t, user)` does the Dex password grant on the `agent-harness` client against `http://localhost:5556/dex/token` with scope `openid email profile groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:warden`, returns the raw ID token and never logs it, the password or the client secret (read from the env file); `cpTraffic(t, query)` GETs the CP `/dashboard/api/traffic?...` (dashboard reads are open today) and decodes events; `agentExec(t, args...)` runs a command in agent-1 through `docker compose exec`; `workerLogs(t)` returns worker-1 logs for token-leak sweeps; `requireStack(t)` (next requirement).
- Own tests (the stack's own proof): `TestIdentityStackBoots` asserts the CP and worker-1 healthz are green, Dex discovery from the host at `http://localhost:5556/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns issuer exactly `http://localhost:5556/dex`, an agent request through the worker to the fake upstream's allowed host succeeds, a request to a non-allowlisted host is denied (default-deny), and a direct no-proxy request from agent-1 fails.
- Blocked, not passed: `requireStack(t)` is the first line of every test in test/e2e/identity (this ticket, DEX-06, IDC-03, IDC-07, SSO-07, GPOL-14, OPS1-10, CSIG-07). When the stack is unavailable (no docker CLI or daemon, compose project not up, Dex unreachable) it calls `t.Fatalf` with a message starting `BLOCKED:` when the environment variable `CI` is `true` (GitHub Actions sets it, so the CI `e2e` job cannot go green on a skip), and `t.Skipf` with a loud message starting `BLOCKED (skipped, not passed):` only when CI is not `true`. The decision is the pure function `stackGate(ci, available bool, reason string) (fail bool, msg string)`, unit-tested without Docker.
- CI: `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` gets a `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity/` step and, after the existing `make e2e` step has torn its stack down, a step running `make e2e-identity`; its `pull_request.paths` filter gains `deploy/compose/dex/**`, `test/e2e/identity/**` (covered by `test/e2e/**` already, keep it explicit if needed) and the new configs; `go test ./tools/riskmap -run TestE2EWorkflowPathsCoverEveryCriticalGlob` still passes. The job id and name stay `e2e`.
- Docs: a short section in docs/docker-end-to-end.md describing `make e2e-identity-*`, the mutual exclusion with `make e2e`, and the helpers. No new architecture class or module is needed (all code is under test/**; no new go.mod dependency).
- No real secret is added: the Dex client secrets and LDAP passwords are the placeholder dev values from deploy/compose/dex/.env.example, and no token, cookie or password is printed by any helper.
- Merging needs the human `gates-change-approved` label because this ticket touches `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`; request maintainer approval when opening the PR.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add docker-compose.e2e-identity.yml and the two config files by copying configs/config.e2e-worker.yaml and configs/config.e2e-cp.yaml; keep them identity-block-free.
2. Add the init service that copies the warden binary into the shared volume and mount it in agent-1; extend test/e2e/hermeticity.sh for dex and ldap.
3. Add the Makefile targets next to the existing e2e targets, with the already-running-stack guard.
4. Create test/e2e/identity/stack_test.go (TestMain), helpers_test.go (dexToken, cpTraffic, agentExec, workerLogs, requireStack, stackGate) and TestIdentityStackBoots, plus TestStackGate.
5. Update .github/workflows/e2e.yml (vet step, second test step, paths) and docs/docker-end-to-end.md; run `go test ./tools/riskmap`.
6. Run `make e2e-identity` locally with Docker, then `make e2e` to prove the base stack still passes after the identity stack was torn down.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity/` is clean, and the default gate never touches Docker: `go test ./...` and `scripts/check.sh` skip the package because every file carries the e2e tag (`go list ./test/e2e/identity` reports `build constraints exclude all Go files`).
- [ ] `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestIdentityStackBoots` passes on a machine with Docker: CP and worker healthy, Dex discovery from the host at `http://localhost:5556/dex` returns issuer `http://localhost:5556/dex` with no dialer override and no /etc/hosts edit, allowed host reachable through the worker, a non-allowlisted host denied, direct egress from agent-1 failing.
- [ ] `test/e2e/hermeticity.sh` passes with dex and ldap running (it is part of `make e2e-identity-up`).
- [ ] `make e2e-identity-up` run while the `warden-e2e` project is already up exits non-zero with the message naming `make e2e-down`.
- [ ] `make e2e` still passes after `make e2e-identity-down` (the base suite is unaffected).
- [ ] `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.e2e.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.e2e-identity.yml config -q` exits 0 with the .env.example values loaded.
- [ ] `go test ./tools/riskmap -run TestE2EWorkflowPathsCoverEveryCriticalGlob` passes; the e2e job runs `make e2e-identity`.
- [ ] `grep -rE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' test/e2e/identity deploy/compose configs` prints nothing and `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] Blocked is not passed, proven without Docker: `go test -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity -run TestStackGate` passes (CI=true with the stack missing yields fail and a message starting `BLOCKED:`; CI unset yields skip and a message starting `BLOCKED (skipped, not passed):`; the stack present yields neither). On a machine with no docker on PATH, `CI=true go test -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity -run TestIdentityStackBoots` exits non-zero and prints `BLOCKED:`, and the same command with CI unset exits 0 and prints `BLOCKED (skipped, not passed)`.
- [ ] `grep -rnE 'dex[C]lient|Dial[C]ontext|/etc/hosts' test/e2e/identity` prints nothing (no test-only dialer, no hosts entry).

### 5/6 · W-P1-DEX-05

**Add scripts/dex-token.sh to fetch and check a seeded user's ID token**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16). The operator docs (W-P1-DEX-03), the Dex runtime proofs (W-P1-DEX-06) and humans trying the recipe all need one way to fetch an ID token for a seeded LDAP user and check its claims. This ticket was split from the original recipe ticket W-P1-DEX-02 (#18). It depends only on W-P1-DEX-01 (the dev Dex config that defines `agent-harness`, the password grant and `audience:server:client_id:warden`). Go-based tests in test/e2e/identity use their own Go helper (`dexToken`, W-P1-DEX-04) and do not shell out to this script. Out of scope: the compose recipe (DEX-02), running Dex (DEX-06).

What to build: `scripts/dex-token.sh <user>` plus a Go test that runs it against an httptest fake token endpoint, so the script is verified without Dex or Docker.

**Requirements**

- New `scripts/dex-token.sh <user> [--raw]` (bash, curl and jq). It reads the user's password only from `DEX_TEST_PASSWORD`, the client secret only from `HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the issuer base from `DEX_URL` (default `http://localhost:5556/dex`, the published dev issuer, so no hosts entry and no `--resolve` are needed on the host; a container that runs the script would set `DEX_URL=http://dex:5556/dex` explicitly because `localhost` is itself there). It fails with a clear message when a variable is missing.
- It runs the password grant with client `agent-harness` and scope `openid email profile groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:warden`, decodes the ID token payload, asserts aud contains `warden`, azp equals `agent-harness` and exp-iat equals 3600, and exits non-zero on any mismatch naming the failed claim.
- By default it prints only decoded claims (sub, email, groups, aud, azp, exp, iat). The raw token is printed only with `--raw` (stdout only, nothing else on stdout). The password, client secret, refresh token and the raw token never appear on stderr or in any message; `set -x` is never used and curl runs without `-v`.
- Dev only: it needs the dev Dex config (password grant). Its header comment says so and that the prod config refuses the grant.
- New test `TestDexTokenScript` in test/deploy/dex_token_script_test.go: an httptest server serves `/dex/token` with canned JWT-shaped tokens (unsigned header.payload.sig built in the test). `DEX_URL` points at the httptest server in every case. Cases: the default URL is `http://localhost:5556/dex` (asserted from the script's usage output, no request made), happy path (claims printed, exit 0), wrong azp, aud without warden, lifetime not 3600, missing password variable, `--raw` prints exactly one line that is the token and without `--raw` the token string appears nowhere in stdout or stderr, and the password and client secret never appear in any output. The test skips with a message when curl or jq is missing and CI is unset, and fails when they are missing and `CI=true`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write test/deploy/dex_token_script_test.go with the fake token endpoint and the cases above; run it and see it fail (script missing).
2. Write scripts/dex-token.sh until the test passes; make it executable.
3. Add the usage block to deploy/compose/dex/README.md (script, env variables, host URL versus container URL).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestDexTokenScript` passes and fails (red first) before the script exists or if the script prints the password, the client secret or, without `--raw`, the token.
- [ ] `ls -l scripts/dex-token.sh` shows an executable file and `bash -n scripts/dex-token.sh` exits 0.
- [ ] `scripts/check-secrets.sh` and `scripts/check.sh` pass (no literal secret in the script).
- [ ] Against a real Dex the script is exercised from the host at the default `http://localhost:5556/dex` by W-P1-DEX-06: `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDexTokenClaims`.
- [ ] `grep -nE 'DEX_RESOLVE|--resolve|/etc/hosts' scripts/dex-token.sh deploy/compose/dex/README.md` prints nothing.

### 6/6 · W-P1-DEX-06

**Prove the Dex recipe at runtime on the L2 identity stack**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue —

Context: feature p1-dex (epic #16). The static tests (DEX-01, DEX-02, DEX-05) prove the Dex files and the token script are well-formed; this ticket proves the recipe actually works when Dex and OpenLDAP run. It holds the runtime checks that the original compose-recipe ticket W-P1-DEX-02 (#18) listed as acceptance, now written as Go tests on the shared stack from W-P1-DEX-04 instead of a WARDEN_IT_DEX integration test. Out of scope: Warden code (nothing here touches the worker or CP), the verifier (p1-verify-token) and the console (p1-sso-roles).

What to build: tests in test/e2e/identity (build tag e2e) named `TestDex*`, so `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestDex` runs them.

**Requirements**

- `TestDexIssuerConsistent`: GET `/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` from the host at `http://localhost:5556` and, from inside the network, with `docker compose exec cp curl http://dex:5556/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` (the internal origin a container uses; this call is made by a container, so it uses `dex:5556` explicitly); both return the same issuer exactly `http://localhost:5556/dex` (split-horizon: the issuer string is fixed by the Dex config, whichever origin is dialled) and a `device_authorization_endpoint`.
- `TestDexTokenClaims`: `scripts/dex-token.sh alice` (default `DEX_URL`, no resolve override, and the .env.example values) exits 0 and shows aud containing `warden`, azp `agent-harness`, groups containing `warden-admins` and `eng`, exp-iat 3600 and `iss` exactly `http://localhost:5556/dex`; for dave groups contain `eng` and no `warden-*` group; the Go helper `dexToken` yields the same claims. A wrong password fails with an error that does not echo the password.
- `TestDexDeviceFlow`: POST to `http://localhost:5556/dex/device/code` with client_id `warden-cli` and scope `openid groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:warden` returns device_code, user_code and verification_uri, and the polling endpoint answers `authorization_pending`.
- `TestDexRestartSurvival`: obtain a token and a refresh token, run `docker compose restart dex`, wait healthy, then verify the earlier ID token's signature against the JWKS now published (using go-oidc is NOT required: check with the standard library and the JWKS keys), and redeem the refresh token for a new ID token.
- No test prints a token, password, client secret or refresh token; failures print claim names and decoded non-secret claims only.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add test/e2e/identity/dex_test.go with the four tests, reusing helpers from W-P1-DEX-04 (each test starts with `requireStack(t)`: blocked fails under CI and skips loudly locally) and the script from W-P1-DEX-05.
2. Run each with `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=<test>` and fix the stack or the recipe if a check fails.
3. Mutation check: change the Dex `idTokens` expiry to 2h in a scratch copy of config.dev.yaml and confirm `TestDexTokenClaims` fails.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME='TestDex(IssuerConsistent|TokenClaims|DeviceFlow|RestartSurvival)'` passes on a machine with Docker.
- [ ] `TestDexTokenClaims` fails (red first) when idTokens is changed from 1h, aud no longer contains `warden`, or alice loses the warden-admins group.
- [ ] `grep -rE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' test/e2e/identity` prints nothing, and the `make e2e-identity` output captured to a file contains no JWT-shaped string: `make e2e-identity 2>&1 | grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` prints 0.
- [ ] `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity/` is clean and `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] Dex is reached with no test-only dialer: `grep -rnE 'dex[C]lient|Dial[C]ontext|--resolve|DEX_[R]ESOLVE' test/e2e/identity` prints nothing, and with the stack missing `CI=true go test -tags e2e ./test/e2e/identity -run TestDexIssuerConsistent` fails with `BLOCKED:`.
